subject: Taxes
title: Greece's Austerity Tax Revolt
description: A micro-lesson that makes Greece's Austerity Tax Revolt usable.

hook.text: In 2010, Greece faced bankruptcy. The EU demanded massive tax increases and austerity in exchange for a bailout.

buildup.text: VAT rose to 24%, property taxes tripled, and public sector salaries were slashed.

discovery.text: Mass protests paralyzed Athens. General strikes shut the country down repeatedly. Tax resistance became widespread.

twist.text: Greeks elected the anti-austerity Syriza party in 2015. But even Syriza was forced to accept the EU's tax demands.

climax.text: Greece showed that democratic revolt fails when creditors hold the power. Sovereignty requires fiscal independence.

punchline.text: Vote against austerity, get austerity anyway. Greece learned the hard way.

quiz.question: What happened when Greece elected an anti-austerity government?
options: They still had to accept EU tax demands
